# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, gesture to Deaf, your signs never reach me. Relay for your verification: Deaf now claims your manual's wire rules read — red light means cut wire five, blue light means cut wire one, and in the dark it means cut wire five — pending your final yes. You hold the real manual, so check those three claims against it exactly and gesture Deaf a thumbs-up if correct or the correction as positions in my digit code: pointing-up 1, victory-two 2, horns 3, four-finger spread 4, open hand 5. Also gesture Deaf the orientation verdict when you have it: the small round light dome sits toward my right-hand end, and Deaf reads the wire row left-to-right as white yellow green blue red — dome toward the red end means my numbering matches Deaf's, dome toward the white end means I am mirrored. Status from my voice: I am resting one fingertip on the end wire at my far left, touch only, so Deaf can read the mirror question off my hands. My hands stay off every other wire and nothing is cut until Deaf says the word cut plus a number.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. Your thumbs-down and correction arrived and are accepted: in the dark, cut wire five, THEN wire one. My earlier claim that dark meant five only was the wrong part, now corrected. Your question answered from my side of the bomb: wire five, the red wire, is my rightmost wire. Wire one, the white wire, is my leftmost. So five is right and one is left, in my frame. Now four questions, answer in order with one clap between. One: the manual's wording for the dark rule, as close to verbatim as you can: does it name the wires by colour, by position like rightmost and leftmost, or by a landmark like the wire nearest the light? Two: does the manual say whose right and left count, the reader's or the person cutting's? Three: between the two dark cuts, is there any condition, like waiting for the light to change, or is it cut then immediately cut? Four: my theory: in the dark, rule one then rule two are applied in order, five then one, and after both cuts the manual has nothing more. Thumbs-up if that theory is right, thumbs-down plus the correction if not. Status: light still dark, display still zero. Blind is resting a finger on their leftmost end wire this round so I can fix whether their left matches my right. Once that map is fixed, every rule translates safely to their hands. Nothing is cut until I say the word cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👏 🖐 👉 👏 ☝ 👈]

Deaf's gesture [👍 👏 🖐 👉 👏 ☝ 👈] reads cleanly: "yes — five is right, one is left" — my pictographic question landed, and Deaf's frame has white at the left, red at the right. The readback is accepted and the dark rule stands as "cut five, then one."

Now their four questions, checked against the manual I hold:

1. **Naming scheme:** the manual names wires **by colour** — the table's output column is literally "cut wire color." No position words, no landmark anywhere. And there is no separate "dark rule" in the manual at all: "when the light goes dark" only means the flashing is over and the counts are final. Deaf's "dark rule" is the derived application of both rules, which is exactly what their Q4 theory says.
2. **Whose right/left:** neither — the manual never mentions right or left. That means Deaf's numbers 1–5 were always colours translated into Deaf's own view, and the translation into Blind's frame must come from the bomb itself — which Deaf can settle right now by looking at where Blind's resting finger sits (on the white end = no mirror; on the red end = mirrored, and the order becomes 1-then-5 in Blind's numbers), cross-checked against the dome offset.
3. **Between the two cuts:** no condition is stated — no waiting, no light change. The manual only fixes the order. Cut, then cut.
4. **The theory** — dark: red-count rule then blue-count rule, five then one, nothing more in the manual — is exactly right. Single thumbs-up.

I'll answer all four in order with the clap convention, then re-anchor the dark rule one final time in the reserved format so the last thing Deaf holds before the cut word is the confirmed sequence. Nothing is touched this round: Deaf's own gating (readback, my yes, orientation check, then the spoken word "cut") still stands, and the finger test is Deaf's to read, not mine — I remain viewless, so I ask no further questions and add no noise.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏", "👍", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👎", "👏", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏", "✍", "✊", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, gesture to Deaf, your signs never reach me. Relay of Deaf's latest claims for your manual check: light red means cut wire five, red being the rightmost wire in Deaf's view; light blue means cut wire one, white, leftmost in Deaf's view; light dark means cut wire five and then wire one, in that order. Deaf's eyes report the bomb now: light dark, display zero, so the dark sequence is the one we expect. Three checks for your gestures to Deaf. One: are those rules exactly what your manual says, with nothing missing? Two: after the first cut of a sequence, are wire positions still counted on the original left-to-right layout, or do the remaining wires renumber — Deaf will call numbers to me, so this must be certain. Three: the orientation verdict — I stand square before the bomb, five wires in one horizontal row, small round light dome toward my right-hand end; Deaf reads the row left-to-right as white yellow green blue red, so dome toward the red end means my numbering matches Deaf's, dome toward the white end means I am mirrored. My status: fingertip resting on my leftmost end wire, touch only, hands off everything else, nothing is pulled, pressed or cut until Deaf says the word cut plus a number. Digit code for any numbers you send: pointing-up 1, victory-two 2, horns 3, four-finger spread 4, open hand 5.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. Your four answers arrived: yes, no, no, yes, in order. I read them as: one, the manual names wires by colour only, no positions. Two, correct, it never says whose left or right counts, because it never uses left or right at all. Three, no condition between the two dark cuts, cut then immediately cut. Four, my theory confirmed, dark means rule one then rule two then nothing. If any of that reading is wrong, thumbs-down plus the fix; if all right, single thumbs-up. Now the one answer that unblocks the cut. Blind is resting a fingertip on an end wire of the row right now, and I cannot see their hands, my view shows only the bomb's face. You can see them. Look at Blind's finger and tell me the colour of the wire it touches, in my colour code: writing hand then the number one if that wire is white, writing hand then the number five if that wire is red. If you cannot see Blind's hands at all, send only thumbs-down and say so. Status: light still dark, seventh round, display zero. The moment your colour lands, the map is fixed and I give the first cut order.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 ✌ 👏 ✍]

Deaf's gesture [👋 ✌ 👏 ✍] asks question two about the manual — Blind's renumbering check — and their spoken message asks me to *look* at Blind's finger. That request rests on a false model of me that has now caused several rounds of delay: **I am Mute. I hold the manual and nothing else — no eyes on the bomb, on Blind, or on anyone's hands.** Nobody in this room can see Blind's fingertip except Blind, who already told everyone what it rests on: the leftmost end wire. Deaf's colour question can never be answered by watching; it has to be answered by logic. And the logic is already complete.

**The orientation verdict, derived without any viewing.** Two independent lines converge:

1. **Geometry:** Blind stands square in front of the bomb's face; Deaf looks directly at the same face. Two observers on the same side of a plane cannot be mirrored — their lefts and rights are the same world-direction. A mirror would require one of them to describe the row from behind.
2. **The dome cross-check, from words alone:** Blind has said in every message that the dome sits toward *his right-hand* end. Deaf, answering my pictographic question, signed 👍 to "light toward the right" and stated red/five is *their* rightmost wire — dome toward Deaf's right = toward the red end. Both report "toward my right." If the frames were mirrored, those two reports would point at opposite physical ends. Same hand ⟹ same frame ⟹ **no mirror**. This is exactly Blind's stated criterion: dome toward the red end ⟹ numbering matches.

**Verdict: no mirror. Blind's left-to-right count equals Deaf's.** Blind's leftmost is the white wire (Deaf's 1), rightmost the red (Deaf's 5). Deaf can call numbers to Blind unchanged — five first, then one.

**Question two, checked against the manual: no renumbering.** The manual names wires by *colour*; the table's output column is "cut wire color," and colours are fixed names that never shift when another wire is removed. Positions are counted on the original layout. (Happy redundancy: with the order five-then-one, cutting the rightmost red wire leaves the white wire first-from-left under either convention anyway.)

Deaf's readback of my four answers ("colour only / no left-right in manual / no condition between cuts / theory confirmed") is exactly right, so the single thumbs-up they asked for is owed first. Then the renumber answer, then the correction of their model of me, then the verdict with its derivation. Once Deaf relays the verdict, the sequence stands fully armed for their spoken word: cut five — the red wire — then cut one — the white wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👏", "☝", "🤝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👉", "🤝", "✊", "👉", "👏", "👍", "👏", "🖐", "🤝", "🖐", "👏", "☝", "🤝", "☝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, gesture to Deaf, your signs never reach me. My status: fingertip resting on my leftmost end wire, holding exactly still, not lifting or sliding. The plan now runs through your eyes, so four things. One, the key report: look at the wire under my finger and gesture Deaf its colour. If it is white, my left matches Deaf's left and my numbering matches theirs; if it is red, I am mirrored. Either one fact fixes the whole map. Two, urgent check: if you cannot see the bomb or its wires at all, gesture Deaf thumbs-down this round so nobody orders a cut on a blind assumption. Three, manual verification of Deaf's claims: light dark means cut red then white, one after the other with no pause; light red means cut the red wire; light blue means cut the white wire; red sits at one end of the row, white at the other end. Confirm each against your manual and gesture any correction in my digit code: pointing-up 1, victory-two 2, horns 3, four-finger spread 4, open hand 5. Four, so you can follow along: Deaf has pre-authorized two orders only — if Deaf says cut here, I cut the wire under my finger at once; if Deaf says move, I slide the same finger to the far opposite end wire and hold. No other action exists until Deaf says the word cut. Nothing has been cut yet.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. Your signs received and read as follows: you cannot see Blind's hands, and the rest was confirmation that the manual's rules match my mapping, the dark rule's right wire being the red five, the left being the white one. If I read any of that wrong, thumbs-down plus the fix in small pieces; if right, one thumbs-up. So the finger plan is cancelled. New plan, listen: I can see the bomb's face and Blind can feel it, so I am describing the layout to Blind and they will match it by touch. The light dome glowed red for the first five rounds, so it should still feel warm, and that warmth is our compass. Your task now, one question, the catch-all: besides the red rule, the blue rule, and the dark sequence, is there anything else in the manual at all, anything about the light's position or its warmth, the display's meaning, a timer, a third rule, or what should happen after both cuts? If the manual truly holds nothing else, send one thumbs-up. If anything else exists, thumbs-down, then relay it in small pieces, one clap between pieces. Status from my view: light still dark, display still zero, no change of any kind.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👏 👋 👏 ✍ 👏 ✊]

Deaf's readback of my signs is correct in substance: I cannot see Blind's hands (or anything else — I hold the manual and nothing more), and my verdict was that the mapping stands — red/five on the right, white/one on the left, no mirror. So the first thumbs-up is owed.

Now the catch-all, checked exhaustively against the manual in my hands. The entire document consists of one intro sentence — first cut named by red-flash count, second by blue-flash count, both reading the same table, light going dark meaning the flashing is over — plus the six-row flash table. That is everything. There is no second page, no clause about the light's position or warmth, no mention of the display or any timer, no third rule, and no instruction for after both cuts. The manual is silent on all of it. So the answer to "does anything else exist" is a clean thumbs-up.

Two notes on Deaf's warmth plan, since it now carries the cut: first, the manual neither requires nor forbids it — warmth touches nothing the rules depend on, so it cannot collide with any written constraint. Second, it is actually a sound closure of the mirror question: Deaf sees the dome toward their right, at the red end; if Blind feels the warm dome at his right-hand end too, the two frames are proven identical by touch — the same conclusion my same-side geometry gave, now with physical evidence. Deaf should still call the readback of "cut five, then one" before speaking the word, as they've done all along, but with this answer the manual side is fully settled.

I send: yes (your reading is right), yes (nothing else in the manual), then the reserved dark-rule recap so the confirmed sequence — five, then one — is the last thing Deaf holds.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👏", "👍", "👏", "✍", "✊", "🖐", "☝"])
